reviewed_non_link.basis: The 2019 AIAA conference paper and the 2018 Cal Poly thesis share a title and substantial text. They remain distinct reports with different publication types, dates, author lists, and identifiers.
The Solar-Stellar Connection journal article and later book chapter have identical abstracts, titles, and authors. They remain distinct publication reports with separate DOIs and venues.
The two Fundamentals of Agile Systems Engineering records share an abstract but explicitly identify Part 1 and Part 2 and have separate DOIs.

The 2016 micropulsed plasma thruster conference paper and journal article have separate DOIs and publication venues. Their abstracts describe closely related versions, so they remain distinct reports.
The 2026 IEEE conference paper has three authors and a conference DOI. The separate 2026 University of Louisiana at Lafayette thesis is solely by Savion Siner.
The 2025 AIAA paper has Steve Simske as a coauthor and a conference DOI. The separate 2025 Colorado State University thesis is solely by Laurence Gregory Magone.
The 2024 IEEE journal article has four authors. The separate 2025 Colorado State University thesis is solely by John M. Gregory.
The SeaLion journal article and thesis have related titles, but they are distinct publication reports with different titles and author lists.
The CubeSat reference-model papers explicitly identify different interim statuses or a separate development-and-distribution report. They are serial updates, not duplicate database manifestations.
The 2021 IAC paper and 2023 journal article on the CNES sustainability index are companion reports with distinct publication manifestations.
The conference and journal versions of the GomX-3 scheduling work have different abstracts and separate DOIs.
The 2011 and 2023 Planetary Interior records are separate encyclopedia editions. The 2014 living entry and its 2015 finalized entry are linked, while both edition records remain separate.

The three conference-proceedings title families each contain multiple distinct records per source. Scopus identifies separate volumes. The available Compendex metadata does not establish safe cross-source volume pairings, so the records remain separate.
Generic labels such as Front Matter, Index, Introduction, Issue Information, and References belong to different books or journal issues. Distinct DOI records with those labels remain separate.
